recipe_cards.name: Beef & Mushroom Stroganoff over Egg Noodles
recipe_cards.nonna_says: Heat a big heavy pan, get it nice and hot. Sear the beef strips fast, two minutes each side, then get them out. Same pan, cook the onions and mushrooms with a pinch of salt until they smell like heaven and all that brown goodness lifts off the bottom. Sprinkle the flour, stir it in, then pour the brandy and let it sizzle. Add your broths, bring it to a gentle bubble, and let the beef finish cooking low and slow for twenty minutes. Cook your egg noodles till they still have a little bite. Off the heat, stir in the sour cream, a squeeze of lemon, the Dijon, and fresh dill. If you're using dried dill from a jar, honey, we need to have a talk.

recipe_cards.name: Baked Ham, Broccoli & Potato Gratin
recipe_cards.nonna_says: Peel your potatoes, cut them into nice chunks, and get them boiling until they're just barely tender. You want them to hold their shape, not turn to mush. While they simmer, melt the butter in a big skillet, soften the onions, then stir in the flour and whisk in the milk until it thickens up and coats the back of a spoon. Toss in the cheddar and stir until it's silky smooth. Fold in the ham and blanched broccoli florets. Pour everything over those potatoes in a buttered baking dish, cover and bake at 350 for half an hour, then uncover and let the top get golden for another fifteen. This is the kind of dish that makes people think you spent all day cooking, so just smile and accept the compliment.

recipe_cards.name: Babo Pasta: Homemade Spinach Pasta with Alfredo Sauce
recipe_cards.nonna_says: Blanch the spinach for thirty seconds, squeeze out every last drop of water, and chop it fine. Make a well in your 00 flour, drop in the egg yolks, the spinach, and a drizzle of olive oil. Work it together with your hands until you've got a smooth, bright green ball of dough, then wrap it tight and let it rest for thirty minutes. Roll it thin through the pasta machine, dust it with flour, and cut your fettuccine. For the sauce, melt butter low and slow, pour in the cream, and stir in a mountain of freshly grated Parmigiano until it's thick and glossy. Cook your pasta in salty boiling water for just two minutes. If you're reaching for the jarred stuff, just close this book and order delivery.

recipe_cards.name: Beef & Broccoli Stir Fry with Oyster Mushrooms
recipe_cards.nonna_says: Slice the flank steak thin against the grain and toss it with soy sauce, Shaoxing wine, and cornstarch. Let it sit while you mix the sauce: oyster sauce, soy, a little sugar, chicken stock, and cornstarch. Blanch the broccoli for thirty seconds until it turns that electric green, then shock it in ice water and drain it dry. Get your wok screaming hot, sear the beef in batches until it's got color but still pink inside, and set it aside. Same wok, hit the garlic and ginger for thirty seconds, add the broccoli and oyster mushrooms, and toss them fast. Pour in the sauce, return the beef, and stir until everything is coated in a sticky, glossy glaze. Serve it over rice immediately because nobody in the history of cooking has ever been sorry for eating this hot.

recipe_cards.name: Broccoli & Oyster Mushroom Flatbread with Ricotta & Chili Honey
recipe_cards.nonna_says: Heat your oven to 450 and get that pizza stone hot if you've got one. Toss the broccoli florets and sliced oyster mushrooms with olive oil, salt, and a pinch of red pepper, then roast them until they're charred and sweet at the edges. Mix the ricotta with lemon zest, a clove of grated garlic, salt, and pepper until it's smooth and spreadable. Stretch your dough thin, spread the ricotta all over, and scatter the charred vegetables on top. Bake until the crust is golden and puffed, about ten minutes. Pull it out and drizzle the hot honey all over while it's still steaming. This is not diet food and it was never trying to be.

recipe_cards.name: Pan-Seared Branzino with Lemon-Herb Butter & Roasted Broccoli
recipe_cards.nonna_says: Pat the branzino fillets bone dry with paper towels, both sides. Season with salt and pepper, nothing fancy. Get your pan hot with a little olive oil, then lay the fillets in skin side down and press them flat with a spatula for the first minute so the skin crisps evenly. Don't touch them for three minutes until the skin is golden and crunchy. Flip gently, cook another two minutes, then take them out. In the same pan, drop in the butter, let it foam and turn just barely golden, then add capers, lemon juice, and a handful of fresh herbs. Spoon that sizzling butter over the fish and serve it next to your roasted broccoli. See? Ten minutes and you've got a restaurant plate.

recipe_cards.name: BBQ Pork Butt with Broccoli Slaw
recipe_cards.nonna_says: Mix your rub the night before: brown sugar, smoked paprika, black pepper, garlic powder, onion powder, mustard powder, and a good amount of kosher salt. Rub the pork butt all over, every crevice, and let it sit uncovered in the fridge overnight so the surface dries out and the flavors sink in. Set up your smoker at 225, add your wood chunks, and put the meat on fat side up. This is a patience game. You're looking at ten to twelve hours until it hits 200 degrees inside and the bone wiggles loose. Pull it out, wrap it in foil, let it rest for an hour, then shred it with two forks. For the slaw, shave the broccoli stems and toss them with shredded cabbage, vinegar, a little sugar, and mayo. The people who tell you barbecue shouldn't take all day have never made anything worth eating.
